html:
SMTO-GIT-0007 — SMTO ignored its saved notes about a Git project

GUID: 06611669-d0f3-48f7-9b54-c3ce25793862
Slug: git-context-invalid
Domain: GIT · Subsystem: git

What happened

  • SMTO keeps short notes about the Git projects used in a conversation. One of those notes was damaged or didn't make sense, so SMTO ignored it. Your project files and Git history weren't touched.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Make sure the Task uses the Gateway where the project lives; you choose the Task's target in the Agent composer. SMTO's notes about a project belong to one Gateway, so a different computer won't have the same project.
  2. Ask SMTO to run git status in the project's top folder. A fresh Git command lets SMTO write new, correct notes to replace the ones it ignored.
  3. If SMTO still describes the project wrongly (wrong folder or remote names), tell it the exact folder path to use. Naming the folder stops SMTO from relying on outdated notes.

What success looks like

  • SMTO describes the project with the right folder and remote names, and this message doesn't come back.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't edit or delete the project's .git folder; the problem is in SMTO's notes, not in your project.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A saved Git working-context record failed validation (field set, Gateway-native absolute path, repository kind, SHA-256 identity or revision, remote list, or preferred-remote consistency) and was discarded.

What this means

  • Saved Git setup validation rejects its exact field set, absolute path, repository kind, digest revisions, remote inventory or preferred-remote consistency. These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.

Why this can happen

  • Saved Git setup validation rejects its exact field set, absolute path, repository kind, digest revisions, remote inventory or preferred-remote consistency.

How to diagnose it

  • Check the named saved field against the current Gateway-native repository and observed remotes.

How to fix it

  • The record is rejected by agent_runtime/native/resource_adapters/git.validate and dropped during conversation working-context normalization; no Git metadata is changed. Run a single, simple Git command (for example git status) in the repository root on the intended Gateway so a fresh setup is recorded, and check the field named in the message if it recurs.
  • Rediscover the repository on the selected Gateway. Review its exact native path, current revision, and remote names before continuing.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Fresh discovery yields a structurally valid setup tied to the intended repository.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • These checks validate repository identity/observation. Failure of an optional observation does not establish failure or rollback of the Git command whose receipt carries it; no diagnostic rewrites Git metadata.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
